newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market falls but traders shrug off tension.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market falls but traders shrug off tension.

text.p: Cyprus stocks fell 1.59 percent on Monday amid renewed tension on the divided island sparked by the killing of a Turkish soldier on Sunday. But floor traders dismissed any suggestion the incident had affected the market.

"It could be a coincidence," said Mary Demetriou, a broker at the Cyprus Investments and Securities Corporation (CISCO) a member of the Bank of Cyprus group. "I did not have people running up to me asking to sell their stock," she added.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) all-share index closed 1.40 points or 1.59 percent lower at 86.60 points compared with Friday's close of 88.0 points.
Volume totalled 789,000 Cyprus pounds ($1.71 million) against 743,000 on Friday.

All five sub-indices fell. Insurance stocks dropped by 2.31 percent, or 1.55 points, to 65.51 while banking stocks, which comprise the largest part of trading on the exchange, fell by 1.71 points, or 1.80 percent, to close at 93.06.
Other traders said the fall was not unusual.
"We had declines last week as well so I do not think what happened had any effect on things," said another broker.

Tension has been running high on the island for the past month - first after the killings of two young Greek Cypriots by people from the other side of the divide in August and now by the shooting incident on Sunday.
The Turkish Cypriot side has blamed Greek Cypriots for the shooting. The Cyprus government has denied the claims.
